class: An email-first gateway's password page was treated as proof that a new employer account existed
symptom: Post Consumer Brands iCIMS accepted the candidate email, showed a login-only page, and the agent tried the ATS password despite no account with this employer. The site refused it. The subsequent reset request produced no mail; the page offered no registration control.
site: Post Consumer Brands Sr. Network Engineer, iCIMS job 32946; output/Post_Consumer_Brands_Sr._Network_Engineer/pages/20261028_162804/page_03.txt and page_04.txt, account/20261028_163958_wrong_password.txt, and live login.icims.com password page on 28 October 2026
root_cause: account_state._knows_account counted email_given as evidence of an account even when the tracker and owner said this employer had no account. next_step selected SIGN_IN on a one-password login page with no Create Account control. Separately, browser_automation.handle_auth_gate and attempt_auto_login could submit the password without consulting the decision table. An email-first login gateway can ask any email for a password, so neither transition establishes an account.
why_tests_missed: The email-first reset tests assumed the site had recognized an existing account, and the no-account tests covered only sign-in pages that offered Create Account. None covered a new employer whose gateway showed only a password form or the direct browser helper path.
fix: For an employer confirmed new, email_given alone no longer establishes an account. A login-only password page without Create Account now stops with a specific registration-path handoff; the browser helper also refuses to type a password on that path. A rejected password on that page does not start another reset. Existing accounts and explicit account-exists messages retain their sign-in and reset paths.
prevention: Test every email-first authentication flow with both known and confirmed new employers, including a gateway that offers no registration control. Do not infer account existence solely from a password prompt.
